next_experiment.reason: The earliest failure is acquisition, and it is isolated by direct mechanical and visual evidence: the jaws travelled to fully closed (pulse 850 to 0) with mechanical_grasp_detected_after_close false, and no frame in either contact sheet shows hanging cloth during the lift, while every far landmark stayed seated. That is an empty close, not a slip and not a whole-garment drag. Because the closure was empty, transport and laydown tested nothing, so pull direction, pull distance, deposit behaviour, and the lift-check ordering carry no evidence against them and stay in keep. The causal hypothesis is geometric rather than merely vertical: the anchor sat on the interior of a single sleeve ply lying flat on the table, where a horizontally closing jaw pair has no lip to capture even though depth reported about 13 mm of local loft. Per the rule against another height-only retry, the change list leads with non-height contact dimensions, contact location, jaw alignment, and entry path, and treats Z only as a consequence of moving to a free boundary.

skill_update.name: flat-ply-edge-engagement
skill_update.purpose: Recognise that closing on the interior of a garment ply that lies flat against the table produces empty jaws even when depth reports several millimetres of local loft, and redirect the next attempt to a verified free fabric boundary.
skill_update.guidance: When a fold step requires lifting a flap that is currently lying flat and fully seated on the table, do not treat reported height above table at an interior point as evidence that the ply can be pinched. A horizontally closing jaw pair needs a fabric lip to capture; on flat interior cloth the jaws simply meet above or through the ply and close on nothing. Before descending, identify a free boundary of the intended flap, such as a hem, cuff, or outer silhouette edge where fabric ends and bare surface begins, and orient the closing axis to cross that boundary so one jaw can pass outside the cloth and the other inside. Read a jaw travel that reaches the fully closed stop together with no mechanical contact signal as direct empty-close evidence, distinct from a slip or from a drag of the whole garment, and confirm it against the hold-check frames for absence of independent hanging material. After such an outcome, change contact location, jaw alignment, and entry path together rather than repeating the same interior descent at a different height, and carry forward the untested transport direction, deposit region, lift-check ordering, and release behaviour unchanged, since an empty closure tested none of them.
skill_update.rationale: This iteration selected a correctly reasoned sleeve anchor with plausible loft and still produced a completely null result, because the failure mode was the closure geometry against flat seated cloth rather than the anchor choice or the planned motion. Existing skills cover null-change recovery and repeated congruent relocations, but none states the flat-ply interior versus free-boundary lesson for fold steps, nor the reading of full jaw travel as empty-close evidence.
